name: crm
title: CRM
summary: Companies, contacts, deals and support tickets per org with pipelines, boards, custom properties, a timeline of activities and tasks, saved views, duplicates and merge, CSV import and export; products, line items and quotes buyers accept on a public link; email sent and logged through people's own Gmail or Outlook with templates; meetings from the calendar; workflows, lead forms, lead scoring, reports, dashboards, a forecast and goals; every record and number is shared through access; teams on HubSpot or Salesforce work their CRM here live through their own connection.
stitch: Decide the default record access for new orgs (crm_settings.record_access defaults to everyone_edits; admins change it in CRM settings) and whether members hold crm.import / crm.delete (defaults: owners and admins) in Settings → Permissions.
Place CRM in the navigation: it ships a main-nav entry and a Home tile on web and a Home entry on mobile. Move it to a mobile tab (expo-router Tabs.Screen for crm/index) if the product is CRM-first.
Link to records from other features with the app paths /crm/companies/<id>, /crm/contacts/<id> and /crm/deals/<id>; notifications and search results already use them.

Adjust the default pipeline (Qualified, Meeting booked, Proposal sent, Negotiation, Won, Lost) and the seeded custom properties to the product's sales motion; bootstrap creates the default pipeline once per org.
Review the copy of record access modes (CRM_RECORD_ACCESS in shared/format.ts) and the lifecycle stages if the team doesn't use HubSpot's terms.

If the agents feature is installed, its per-resource scopes apply to CRM records through access (crm.team and crm.workspace are their parents); nothing to wire. Without it, agents get the user's own level capped at edit.

Pick each workspace's CRM in CRM settings → Connected CRMs (app, connected or both; default app) and which platforms people may connect. Connecting accounts needs the connectors feature (2.0) with HubSpot/Salesforce OAuth apps registered for this deployment; without it the CRM works as before and offers no connected sources.

Calendar (optional): call crm.SetMeetingSource(fn) with the caller's events that include any of a contact's addresses in a time range, and crm.SetBookingLinks(fn) with the caller's booking pages. Without them "Log meeting" and the {{booking_link}} merge field are hidden; everything else works.

Link cards (optional): register crm.Unfurl(ctx, viewer, path) (the package-level form of (*crm.Service).Unfurl) with a messaging feature's link-card seam (channels: RegisterUnfurler("/crm/", …)) and map crm.LinkCard onto its card type; it applies the record route's checks and returns nil when the viewer can't open the record.

Email: the CRM sends and reads mail only through connections the connectors feature offers with its capabilities (crm.google.mail_read/mail_send, crm.microsoft.mail_read/mail_send). Register Gmail (gmail.readonly, gmail.send) and Microsoft Graph (Mail.Read, Mail.Send, Mail.ReadWrite) scopes on the deployment's OAuth apps; Gmail's read scope is restricted and needs Google's verification and security assessment before external users can use "Log to CRM". Google connections may list a "gmail" endpoint (else it's derived from "drive").

Public quote and form pages: the wire lines add /q/(.*) and /forms/(.*) to the web proxy's public paths and let /forms/:token be framed by other sites for embeds. Decide who holds crm.publish_quotes (members by default), crm.manage_forms and crm.manage_workflows (admins).
